reviews.reason:
Reading: the real image is a BSE micrograph of Ti-6Al-4V. It shows dark alpha laths separated by thin bright beta ribs, arranged in columnar prior-beta grains with basketweave and colony regions. Flakes between thin lines is therefore the right reading, with moderate confidence (~70%). The phase reading would give nearly the same objects. The problem is how well the reading is executed.

Failures on the real image:
(1) Merging across boundaries. In the upper half, single large blue, cyan and green regions span many parallel laths and even cross colony boundaries. Examples are the large green band running diagonally through the centre and the cyan blocks at the top centre.
(2) Cutting along length. In the lower third, the laths are cut into short stubby fragments (red, magenta and orange blobs). The median AR of 2.19 is implausibly low for Ti-64 alpha laths. This matches the twin's aspect-ratio bias of -51%.
(3) Grey/unused regions are numerous and coverage is 0.69, so many genuine laths are discarded.
(4) A scratch is reported at about x=1175, y=250-340. No scratch is visible in the micrograph there; it appears to be a lath edge detected as a scratch (false positive).
(5) Colony boundaries: the V-shaped prior-beta columns are visible in the micrograph. The colour map follows them only roughly, and merged regions bleed across them.
The global S=0.43 may be roughly right for a mixed basketweave, but per-flake AR and misalignment are not supported by the drawing.

Twin: the twin is untrusted, since a single uniform field of parallel lamellae does not resemble the columnar basketweave. Even on the twin the method fails:
- The true diagonal scratch (~40°) is not marked. Instead, two scratches are drawn parallel to the flake direction (~117°), i.e. along lamellae. This fits scratch recall_crossing of 0.29.
- The lamellae are broken at the bright dots into short pieces: flake recall 0.46, precision 0.33, AR bias -0.51.

Previous runs on the same set also failed (rotation check 0.45, holdout worst family 7.5). The evidence does not support the measured numbers.

reviews.reason: Reading: in this BSE image of Ti-6Al-4V the alpha laths are the mid-grey bands and the beta is the thin bright ribs between them. Confidence in the reading is moderate (~65%); a phase reading with bright beta as the matrix would outline nearly the same laths. The numbers are not supported, for four reasons. (1) The laths are cut along their length. The upper colonies hold laths hundreds of px long and a few px wide, yet the median aspect ratio is 2.1, and the drawing shows long laths broken into short segments. The twin confirms this as a systematic bias: aspect-ratio bias -0.58, flake recall 0.22, flake precision 0.10, and the twin drawing shows each lamella chopped into short blobs (AR 1.7). (2) Coverage is only 0.66. Many grey (unused) regions sit inside clean colonies, especially in the lower fine band, so S=0.41 and the local S come from a biased subset. I cannot judge from the drawing whether 0.41 is right; it is plausible for a multi-colony field but not verified. (3) Scratches: the real image shows no visible scratch and none is drawn; the vertical white line at about x=1175 is the mean-direction arrow (88°), not a scratch. On the twin, the obvious diagonal bright scratch was missed (scratches 0, crossing recall 0.0), so scratch handling is untested at best. reviews.reason:
Confidence about 0.7. The real micrograph looks like a back-scattered electron image of lamellar TiAl/Ti. Lamellae appear as strips of several grey levels (white, light grey, dark grey, black) that touch each other. There are no thin dark boundary lines between them. The boundary reading (flakes between thin lines) therefore has nothing reliable to follow, and the regions reading is the one a metallographer would use.

What the drawing shows:
- Within colonies, the colour (orientation) is broadly coherent: magenta upper-left and centre, cyan/blue lower half, orange right. The mean direction and S=0.56 are therefore plausible at colony scale.
- Many coloured regions are wide blocks that span several lamellae, for example the large purple and magenta patches and the blue blocks at the upper right. The fine white and dark lamellae in the lower half are partly merged into broad bands.
- A median aspect ratio of 2.96 is not credible for lamellae that look roughly 10:1 or more by eye. This fits flakes being merged across their width. It also matches the twin's aspect-ratio bias of -0.30 (aspect ratio underestimated).
- Equiaxed blocky regions (green and orange at the right, grey patches) are partly coloured and counted. Some of them look like globular or grain-boundary alpha rather than lamellae.
- There is one long thin white line inside the magenta colony. It is either a false scratch or the mean-direction arrow. No real scratch is evident in that image, so scratch handling on the real set cannot be judged.

Twin:
- It is flagged untrusted, and rightly so. It shows dark rounded flakes in a light matrix with drawn boundary lines, which is a phase-in-matrix structure unlike the real image. Its scores say little about the real set.
- Even on its own terms it fails. Worst family tolerance ratio is 2.78. Flake precision is 0.69. Scratch recall is 0.002 and scratch precision is 0.03. The obvious horizontal scratch at the upper right is drawn as red flake fragments and reported as scratches0.

The same set (tial_lamellar_L26, distance 0) failed before under the boundary reading. Its rotation check of 0.974 shows only that the result is stable, not that it is correct. The drawings do not support the reported aspect ratio, the flake count, or the misalignment. They do not show that scratches are found or kept from cutting flakes.
reviews.next_step: Switch reading: boundaries -> regions. Flakes should be separated by steps between grey levels, using multi-level quantisation or a watershed on the gradient magnitude. Number of grey levels: auto -> 4. Set the minimum flake width near the fine scale found in the flake phase (about 18 px) so that thin lamellae are not merged into the coarse (about 79 px) blocks. Exclude compact regions as non-lamellar: compactness/aspect-ratio filter, aspect ratio min 1.5 -> 3. Rebuild the twin as BSE-like touching lamellae with 3–5 grey levels, no matrix and no boundary lines, so it can become trusted. Then re-tune scratch detection on that twin, since current scratch recall of about 0 means scratch handling is broken regardless of reading. If the regions reading still gives a median aspect ratio below about 5 on the real image, no parameter of the current method can fix the merging, and the image should be marked unsupported.

reviews.reason:
Reading (confidence about 0.7): the regions reading fits the real image. It is a BSE-type TiAl/Ti lamellar micrograph in which strips of 3–4 grey levels touch without dark separating lines. The drawing colours the colonies coherently: steep cyan/blue in the lower half, magenta/purple diagonal in the upper middle, orange/green in the right, with grey for the equiaxed dark patches at top right. The mean direction and the colony split are therefore plausible.

The drawings do not support the numbers, for three reasons.

(1) Twin, which is the only place with truth: worst tolerance ratio is 1.97 and worst family 2.56, both above 1. Flake recall is only 0.55. Aspect ratio has a +29% bias, and the bias equals the relative error, so it is systematic overestimation. The twin drawing shows why. Adjacent same-orientation flakes are merged into blobs, e.g. the magenta/purple H-shaped region centre-left and grey merged clumps along the colony boundaries. Collinear flakes are also joined end to end. Both raise the aspect ratio and lower recall.

(2) Scratches: the header says scratches0, and none of the three bright scratches is drawn as a white line. Instead they are segmented as thin orange/red flakes, and they cut the lamellae they cross. The listed scratch precision 0.95 / recall 0.90 cannot belong to this drawing. Either the scores are from a different configuration or split, or the drawing is wrong. This must be resolved before any score is trusted.

(3) Real image: no scratches are visible, so that part cannot be checked. In the fine-lamella band at the bottom (fine width about 18 px against coarse about 79 px), the coloured strips look wider than the individual white/black lamellae in the micrograph. I am unsure at this resolution, but it suggests neighbouring fine lamellae are merged, which would inflate AR (4.37) and lower S. Several large white equiaxed patches on the left are coloured as flakes rather than grey, so possible grain-boundary/globular alpha is taken as flakes. Coverage is 0.67.

No rotation check is reported for this regions configuration. The earlier 0.974 was for the boundary reading on L26. The twin is untrusted, so even a pass there would say little about this image.

Confidence the result is not acceptable: about 0.85.

reviews.reason:
The real image is a TEM bright-field micrograph of bainite (0.2 µm bar). It shows bright ferrite between discrete dark lenticular plates at roughly 30°. The plates vary in width, taper and stop part-way, so they are not continuous thin boundary lines. That makes the boundary reading a poor fit: the bright regions are a connected matrix, not closed flakes. I judge the phase reading, with the dark plates as flakes in a bright matrix, more appropriate (confidence about 55–60%). History supports switching: bainite_L06, at distance 0.0, already failed with the boundary reading (rotation check 0.68).

What the drawing shows on the real image:
(a) Bright laths merge wherever a dark plate ends. Several yellow and orange fills run across two or three neighbouring laths.
(b) The large dark band in the centre-right is filled olive and counted as one big flake, so a matrix-like dark region enters the statistics.
(c) Green patches sit across the laths at a different orientation colour. Laths are cut crosswise into fragments, which explains the median aspect ratio of 2.29. The visible laths look to be about 5–10 times longer than wide.
(d) In the cluttered top-centre region, many small red, magenta, blue and green fragments are coloured and counted.
(e) In the featureless top-left area the large regions are mostly grey, but the teal block is coloured and therefore used.

The colony-level mean direction looks plausible: the arrow follows the laths and the dominant yellow colour fits about 30°. Per-flake aspect ratio and the flake count (330) are not supported by the drawing. S = 0.78 is probably pulled down by the spurious fragments.

The twin does not help here. It is untrusted and looks like the phase reading (bright rods in a dark speckled matrix), not this image. Its scores are poor: flake precision 0.54, recall 0.71, aspect-ratio bias -20%, worst family ratio 2.19. Its scratch_recall is 0 and its header shows 0 scratches, although several bright scratches clearly cut the rods; in the drawing these scratch lines split rods and merge pieces across them. The real image shows no polishing scratches, so scratch handling cannot be judged on it.
reviews.next_step:
Switch the reading from boundaries to phase, with the flake phase going bright -> dark. Treat the dark lenticular plates as flakes and the bright ferrite as matrix.

Parameter changes (exact names depend on the config):
- minimum flake area: raise to about 150–200 px, to drop the top-centre clutter fragments.
- elongation (aspect-ratio) threshold for counting a flake: raise to about 2.5, so the blocky dark band and equiaxed blobs go grey.
- low-texture or featureless-region mask: enable it, so the top-left grey area is excluded from flakes.
- dark-phase gap closing: if plates fragment along their length, add a small directional closing of about 3 px.

Regenerate the twin as thin, tapered dark plates in a bright matrix with discontinuous ends, so that it becomes trusted. Then rerun the rotation check. Accept only if the median aspect ratio rises toward the visible 5–10 and the rotation check improves well above 0.68.

If the phase reading also merges plates where they touch, no parameter of the current method may fix it; report the orientation and S at colony level only, and withhold per-flake aspect ratio.

reviews.reason:
Reading: the dark lenticular plates in bright ferrite are what a metallographer would measure. Most coloured fills lie on those plates, which run at about 30°, and the bright ferrite stays unfilled. So the phase reading with the dark phase is right (about 75% confident). One inconsistency should be checked: the two-scale report labels the flake phase 'bright' (area share 0.35), which conflicts with the stated dark-phase reading.

Where the drawing fails on the real image:
(1) Plates are cut along their length. Many long yellow and green plates are split by cross-cuts into 2–4 segments, and short orange or red stubs sit at the plate tips. This is why the median aspect ratio is 2.08, while visible plates have length-to-width ratios of roughly 8–15. The reported AR is therefore not supported.
(2) Non-plate dark material is taken as flakes. The broad dark band at lower centre is filled with large blocky green, yellow and purple patches. The dark, mottled region along the top edge (dislocation contrast and the upper grain) is broken into dozens of small irregular, multicoloured blobs that are coloured, so they are counted. They should be grey (excluded) or left unsegmented. These blobs add random orientations, so the order parameter S = 0.80 is probably biased low, and the 304 'used' flakes are inflated.
(3) A false scratch: a white scratch line is drawn in the centre, parallel to the plates. A TEM foil has no polishing scratches, so this is a false positive. It may also be cutting or merging plates where it lies.
(4) The mean direction (about 30°) and the colony-level colouring look right.

Twin: it scores well, but its plates are uniform rounded rods in tidy colonies. It has no tapered lenticular plates, no mottled dislocation-contrast regions and no wide dark bands, so its good AR error (2.6%) does not carry over to this image. Its scratch recall on crossings is 0.31, so scratch handling is weak anyway.

Confidence that the measured AR and the flake count are wrong: high. Confidence that the direction is right: moderate-high.

The search space varies the parameters most likely to control plate width and splitting: threshold offset, smoothing, watershed and merge settings, and the area floor.

Confidence that this improves the drawing: moderate, about 50%. If plates that touch still merge in the phase reading, per-flake aspect ratio should be withheld and only colony-level direction and S reported.

reviews.reason: Reading: the phase reading is the right family, but the wrong phase was chosen. The micrograph is labelled primary cementite (white cast iron). What a metallographer measures are the long, straight, bright primary-cementite plates. They run up to roughly 1 mm, are tens of µm thick, and cross each other at many angles. In the drawing those plates are left white and unmeasured. The coloured 'flakes' are something else: dark pearlite and ledeburite islands and dots in the eutectic background, plus dark etch and pull-out patches. Some of those patches are shown in grey, and some are wrongly coloured as large irregular purple, orange and olive blobs. So all 10,015 'flakes' and the summary numbers describe the wrong objects. S = 0.035, AR 2.06 and coverage 0.345 are numbers for the eutectic texture, not for the plates. An S near 0 might even be roughly true for the plates, but it was not measured on them, so it cannot be claimed. Failures seen: (a) Matrix and eutectic islands are taken as flakes, everywhere. (b) The real flakes are missed completely. (c) Large dark etch stains are counted as flakes. (d) Scratches: one short line near the centre is marked as a scratch. I cannot confirm it is a real scratch; it looks like part of a plate edge. Twin: it is untrusted and does not resemble this image (short dark dashes in grey colonies versus long bright crossing plates). Its own scores are also poor: flake precision 0.03, crossing-scratch recall 0.05, aspect-ratio bias -41%, worst family 3.5× tolerance. It gives no support to any number. The closest earlier set (needles_L23, distance 0.0, same reading) failed: holdout 4.2×, rotation check 0.70. Confidence that the reading is wrong: high, about 90%. Confidence that no number in this run is usable: high.
reviews.next_step: Change the reading to the other phase: flake_phase: dark -> bright. Also raise the minimum flake size so the fine bright cementite inside the ledeburite is not taken. Set min_flake_area to about 10× its current value, and require a minimum flake length of about 100 µm and aspect ratio ≥ 4 for 'used' flakes. Add a light morphological opening (radius about 3–5 px) before labelling, to detach the plates from the bright eutectic network. Crossing plates will merge into X and star shapes. To handle them, enable splitting of branched objects at junctions (skeleton split, or a line or Hough-based plate fit) instead of greying them out. Otherwise the branched filter will discard most of the plates. Rebuild the twin to match this image: long bright plates 5–40 px thick, random crossings, a dark mottled eutectic background with dark stains. Only then re-tune on the twin, and require the rotation check to beat 0.3 before accepting. If the method's labelling cannot split crossing plates, say that no current parameter fixes this, and measure plate orientation with a line or structure-tensor approach on the bright mask instead.

reviews.reason:
Phase reading is correct for this image: the long bright primary-cementite needles in the ledeburite matrix are the flakes. The coloured regions in the drawing do lie on those bright needles. That contradicts the stated 'flakes are the dark phase', so the polarity setting needs checking.

The drawings do not support the numbers:
(1) Long needles are cut along their length into several pieces, and the pieces sometimes get different colours. This happens mostly where needles cross each other, e.g. top-right orange/purple needles and the centre yellow/magenta pair.
(2) Many clearly visible needles stay grey, so they are not used. Coverage is only 0.19, and several near-horizontal needles in the left half are missing.
(3) Many small coloured specks in the eutectic/ledeburite regions are matrix lamellae taken as flakes. They make up much of n=359 and pull the median aspect ratio down to 2.1, whereas the visible needles have aspect ratios of roughly 15–50. The aspect-ratio figure is wrong by about an order of magnitude.
S=0.21 (near-random needle network) is plausible, but its value is uncertain given the contamination. No scratches are visible, and none were reported. Colony/grain boundaries are not the issue here; crossings between needles are.

The twin is useless as evidence. Its short-dash colonies do not resemble crossing needles. Flake recall is 0, its drawing shows dashes merged into large grey blobs, and it is untrusted.

The closest prior set, needles_L23 (distance 0, same reading), also failed: rotation check 0.70, holdout worst family 4.2. Repeating that configuration will not succeed.

Confidence: high that this should be rejected; moderate on the exact causes.
reviews.next_step:
Parameter names below are illustrative; map them to the method's actual names.
(a) Set flake polarity: dark -> bright, so the stated reading matches what is segmented.
(b) Raise min_flake_area by about 5–10x, to roughly the area of a needle 3 widths long, and require minimum aspect ratio for use 1.5 -> 4. This drops the ledeburite specks.
(c) Split at crossings by orientation rather than merging or fragmenting there: enable skeleton/branch splitting with an angle threshold of about 15°, and re-join collinear fragments across gaps of up to 2 needle widths (merge_collinear: off -> on, max_angle 10°).
(d) Regenerate the twin as long, straight, randomly oriented crossing needles (width 5–20 px, length 200–1500 px) on a fine eutectic-textured matrix, and do not score until it is trusted.
If (b) and (c) cannot both keep crossing needles separate and remove matrix fragments, state that the current method cannot measure needle aspect ratios on this set.

plans.hypothesis: The rejected drawing measured the wrong phase. Switching flake_phase from dark to bright should make the coloured flakes coincide with the long bright primary-cementite plates on the next review. This also needs three more changes: raising min_area_px about 10x and min_aspect_for_orientation to 3, so ledeburite dots are dropped; turning off the grain-boundary-alpha filter, so long plates are not greyed out; and turning off scratch detection, so plates are not inpainted as scratches. The claim is falsified if the reviewer again sees the plates left unmeasured, or sees them fused with the bright eutectic network into large branched blobs.
plans.rationale:
The only evidence is the reviewer's reading of the real drawing. It judged the phase family correct but the phase wrong, with about 90% confidence: the dark pearlite and ledeburite islands were measured, and the bright cementite plates were left white. The twin is untrusted (contrast ratio 0.42, minority fraction ratio 0.58), and its scores (precision 0.03, worst family 3.5x tolerance) support nothing, so no twin search runs and these start params go straight to review. I change only params tied to the reviewer's evidence:
- flake_phase: dark -> bright, as the reviewer directed.
- min_area_px: 19 -> 200, about 10x as asked, to drop the fine bright cementite inside the ledeburite.
- min_aspect_for_orientation: 1.5 -> 3.0. The reviewer asked for >= 4, but 3 is the maximum this param accepts.
- gb_alpha_length_factor: 4 -> 0 (off). Primary plates are by nature much longer than the median flake and cross their neighbours at large angles, so the default rule would grey them out as grain-boundary alpha.
- detect_scratches: off. The one detected 'scratch' looked to the reviewer like a plate edge, and long straight bright plates are exactly what the scratch detector would inpaint away.
- sigma: 0.8 -> 1.5, to smooth the fine bright eutectic texture.
- phase_offset: 0.05, to thin the bright mask slightly so plates detach from the eutectic network. This is the closest available stand-in for the requested morphological opening.

Limitations stated plainly:
- The method has no opening and no junction-splitting param. Crossing plates will form X and star shapes. The skeleton branch_test will leave such shapes out of the statistics rather than split them, so orientation coverage of the plates may stay poor. No current parameter fixes this; a line or structure-tensor fit on the bright mask would be needed.
- Bright is the majority phase here (about 0.55), so the eutectic cementite network may still merge with the plates.
- The nearest earlier set (needles_L23) failed under the same reading.

Confidence: about 60% that the coloured objects will at least be cementite after this change, and about 25% that the drawings will be accepted. No number from this run should be claimed until the twin is rebuilt to look like long bright crossing plates and the rotation check beats 0.3.

plans.hypothesis: Raising min_area_px from 200 to 500, raising phase_offset from 0.05 to 0.10, and narrowing merge_max_offaxis_deg from 30 to 15 will remove most coloured eutectic and ledeburite specks. The next drawing should then show a median aspect ratio above 4 and S measured mostly on needles. Needles cut or greyed where they cross will remain, because no parameter in this method splits crossing plates by orientation.
plans.rationale: Both reviews agree on the reading: phase, with the bright primary-cementite needles as the flakes. The current best already uses flake_phase=bright, so the reading and phase stay as they are. The twin is untrusted (minority fraction ratio 0.58, contrast ratio 0.42, flake recall 0, precision 0.03), so its scores support nothing and these start params will be judged only by the next review of the real drawing. I therefore change only three params, each tied to something the reviewer saw. (1) Specks of matrix lamellae dominate n=359 and pull the median aspect ratio down to 2.1. min_area_px goes to 500, the maximum allowed; this is a 2.5x increase rather than the 5-10x the reviewer suggested, because 500 is the cap. min_aspect_for_orientation stays at 3.0; the reviewer suggested 4, but the parameter's maximum is 3. (2) A slightly higher phase_offset, 0.10, thins the bright mask so that plates detach from the bright eutectic network. The reviewer suggested a morphological opening, which this method does not offer; this is the closest available control. (3) Needle pieces get different colours at crossings, a sign that pieces of crossing needles are merged off-axis. merge_max_offaxis_deg=15 restricts merges to pieces lying end to end, close to the reviewer's request to re-join only collinear fragments. Not changed, and stated plainly: no parameter splits X-shaped crossings by orientation. The skeleton branch test will still grey out merged crossings, and the watershed will still cut needles at crossings, so coverage will likely stay low (perhaps 0.2-0.35). The aspect-ratio and length numbers for the needles will very probably remain unusable. If the next review still shows crossings cut or greyed, the honest conclusion is that this method cannot measure needle aspect ratio on this set; at most a structure-tensor S, or tensor_order_parameter on the bright mask, could be reported. The closest earlier set, needles_L23 (distance 0), failed (rotation check 0.70, holdout worst family 4.2), which supports low expectations. Confidence: about 60% that the specks drop substantially, and about 15% that the run is accepted.
